answer: Shortlist three companies through referrals and targeted searches, then vet each one: pull its WCB clearance, ask for a certificate of liability insurance, search its name in the Companies Office, call two or three commercial references, and get a detailed written quote after a site visit. Walk away from pressure, large cash deposits or skipped permits.

blocks.x: Finding commercial renovation contractors used to mean asking around. Today, many business owners start with a Google search, a review site or even an AI assistant like ChatGPT. That makes it easy to get a list of names, and harder to know how to vet a commercial contractor in Winnipeg before you hand over a deposit.
Where to look

**Referrals.** Ask property managers, commercial real estate agents, architects and other business owners who renovated recently. A referral from someone with a similar project is still the best starting point.

**Google and maps.** Search for your project type plus Winnipeg (for example, "office renovation Winnipeg" or "restaurant renovation Winnipeg"). Look past the ads, and don't judge a company by its website alone. Ask for references and run the public-record checks below.
**AI assistants.** Tools like ChatGPT can suggest names, but they draw on what's publicly written online. Treat their suggestions as a starting list, not a recommendation, and verify everything.
**Industry groups.** Local construction and home builders' associations list their members.
Build a shortlist of three
For each candidate, check:
**Commercial work like yours:** offices, retail, clinics, restaurants. Ask how many they've finished recently. Residential-only experience isn't the same.
**Reviews that mention specifics:** schedules met, communication, cleanliness, working around customers.
**Public records:** look the business up in the [Manitoba Companies Office](https://companiesoffice.gov.mb.ca/) registry, and make sure the name there is the one on the quote.
**How quickly they respond** to your first inquiry. It's a preview of the project.
How to vet a commercial contractor before you sign

**WCB Manitoba clearance.** Hire a firm that isn't in good standing and you might be liable for its assessment costs, WCB Manitoba warns. A [clearance letter](/blog/how-to-check-a-contractors-wcb-clearance-manitoba) is open to anyone through WCB's public Clearance Request System, so pull one before work starts and again before each payment.
**Liability insurance.** Request a certificate of insurance with you named as certificate holder, and confirm it with the listed insurer or broker.
**References** from two or three commercial clients. Call them.

**Permit experience** on projects like yours in Winnipeg. You can look up a property's issued permits in the [City's permit search](https://ppdportal.winnipeg.ca/Permits/PropertyPermitSearch/Start.jsp).

**A detailed written quote** with scope, allowances, schedule, payment terms and warranty. The payment terms should allow for [Manitoba's 7.5% builders' lien holdback](/blog/builders-lien-holdback-manitoba).
**Site visit first.** A serious contractor won't give a firm commercial price without seeing the space.
Questions that reveal experience
How will you keep my business open during construction?
What permits will we need, and how long does review usually take?
What surprises do you typically find in buildings like mine?
Who is my single point of contact on site?
Red flags
Pressure to sign quickly or pay large cash deposits
No written contract
Suggestions to skip permits
Reluctance to provide clearance, insurance or references
Payment instructions that change by email
The bottom line
Search tools make it easy to find commercial renovation contractors. Vetting them on experience, references and clear written terms is what protects your project.
